extracted.intended_audience: novelists, literary critics, and students of literature
extracted.subtask_description: Principles for writing and judging the novel focused on perception, execution, and the novel's capacity to present a convincing impression of life. Applies to creation (selection, form, sensibility) and to critical evaluation (solidity, coherence, execution).

rubrics_metrics.name: Be interesting
rubrics_metrics.description: The novel's only obligation is to be interesting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Central doctrine: 'The novel is "a personal, a direct impression of life." Its only obligation is to be interesting.' There are no a priori rules; interest derives from the quality of perception and execution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novel as a personal, direct impression of life
rubrics_metrics.description: 'A novel is a personal, a direct impression of life: that, to begin with, constitutes its value.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value is rooted in the author's individual impression and presentation of life; this personal execution is what critics may legitimately measure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freedom from rules / Reject prescriptive formulas
rubrics_metrics.description: A novel must be free to be what it is; prescriptive formulas and dictated subjects are to be rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: James argues against Walter Besant's prescriptive lecture: 'There are no a priori rules.' Critics should not impose subjects or rigid prescriptions on novelists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solidity of specification (the air of reality)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'The air of reality (solidity of specification) seems to me to be the supreme virtue of a novel.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete, sensory detail and specificity create an 'air of reality'; without this solidity, other merits collapse. Emphasize concrete particulars and sensory reality to sustain reader belief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coherence and organicity (novel as living organism)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'A novel is a living thing, all one and continuous... in proportion as it lives will it be found... that in each of the parts there is something of each of the other parts.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parts should reflect the whole; character and incident are inseparable ('What is character but the determination of incident? What is incident but the illustration of character?'). Aim for organic unity where every element interrelates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of perception / acute observation
rubrics_metrics.description: Cultivate the most acute perception possible: 'Try to be one of the people on whom nothing is lost.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The writer's task is to register, observe, and discriminate. High-quality perception produces distinctive, precise detail and informed selection of material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection and form
rubrics_metrics.description: The novelist's intelligence is shown in what is selected for treatment and in the proportions given to each element.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judgment about which incidents, scenes, or traits to include and how much attention to allocate is central to the craft; good selection and proportion produce a balanced, effective whole.

rubrics_metrics.name: Execution as the proper subject of criticism
rubrics_metrics.description: 'The execution belongs to the author alone; it is what is most personal to him, and we measure him by that.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criticism should focus on how the novelist realizes material (style, perception, structure), not on dictating what subjects the novelist ought to write about.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honesty of impression
rubrics_metrics.description: A novel should convey an honest impression rather than an affected or contrived one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed among evaluative criteria; honesty of impression ties to the authenticity and integrity of the author's perception and presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experience as sensibility
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Experience is never limited, and it is never complete; it is an immense sensibility, a kind of huge spider-web of the finest silken threads suspended in the chamber of consciousness.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The writer's experience is an expansive sensibility that notices fine particulars; cultivating broad, subtle sensibility enriches perception and the material available for fiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject autonomy (critics should not judge subject matter)
rubrics_metrics.description: The subject of a novel is the writer's province alone and may not properly be dictated by critics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While critics evaluate execution, they should not prescribe or condemn a novelist's choice of subject; judgment should be reserved for how subjects are handled.
